strategyReview: Weekend Hyperliquid funding-reversion long continues to be our strongest signal, with 72% live win rate and 0.40% average PnL on 337 trades. One-touch NO sell-YES edge (live) has perfect 4/4 record with outsized gains, and its shadows show +1.28% average PnL over 233 resolved. Funding-extreme signals break even, with long side struggling on AMZN and HYPE. Polymarket IV-touch rich NO shadows perform well (79% win, +2.26 total) and are candidates for promotion. Failing: shadow-mined heatmap/cluster signals (gold one-touch NO heatmap 0/16, no-bias gap shadow 43% win), cross-asset momentum confirmation (HYPE confirming BTC 0/8), and the AMZN perp/spot convergence family (43% scorable win, many unscorable variants). These failures show that backtested shadow edges on gold heatmaps and cross-asset BTC-HYPE co-movement are not replicating forward.

failureClusters.evidence: Gold one-touch NO heatmap (H-534) is 0/16, no-bias adjusted gap shadow (NB family) 43% win with average -1.26%. Both showed strong backtest profiles (e.g., heatmap WR 58% n=12) but fail in forward tests.
failureClusters.recommendation: Stop promoting further shadow-mined heatmap / gap variants until we understand the forward failure mechanism; suspect noise patterns discovered by the mining run.

failureClusters.evidence: The family that longs BTC when HYPE confirms risk-on (H-108 etc.) is 0/8, all tests resulting in BTC declines (e.g., -1.62%). HYPE spot above SMA and stable OI did not predict BTC outperformance.
failureClusters.recommendation: Retire the HYPE-BTC confirmation thesis as currently formulated; if revisiting, require much tighter directional alignment on BTC itself before allowing HYPE as a filter.

failureClusters.evidence: The AMZN perp/spot convergence family has 16/37 scorable tests (43% win) and 83 unscorable burn tests. Many variants expect convergence from positive funding/near-zero basis, but funding often stagnates or stays near 5.5%, yielding no directional move.
failureClusters.recommendation: Kill the current positive-funding convergence variants and refocus on extreme negative funding/basis reversion where the mispricing is large enough to force a meaningful spot move.

hypothesisReviews.observation: Primary variant of gold one-touch NO heatmap (gold_pm_underlying_cap_edge_pts_max >= 10 predicting >2% spot decline in 2 days) went 0/16 in forward testing. The large edge came from YES overpricing relative to the underlying cap, but gold spot declined only modestly and never reached the 2% threshold. No accompanying momentum or funding signal was required, so the edge alone did not translate into directional spot moves.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large underlying-cap edge on gold one-touch NO contracts reliably predicts >2% spot decline within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: BTC PM IV expansion reversion (PM IV < 46, opt IV > 49, ratio < 0.92 predicting >2% abs move in 3 days) produced only 30% win rate. Early wins were driven by genuine breakouts, but later tests show that even when PM IV is low, spot often chopped in a tight range, failing to hit the 2% move. The absolute IV thresholds are not stable across different BTC regimes.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC PM IV below 46 while options IV remains high guarantees a >2% absolute spot move within 3 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: Cross-asset IV compression vol expansion primary variant (BTC trending with HYPE confirming) resulted in 0/8, all losses (BTC -1.62%). HYPE spot SMA alignment and stable OI did not predict BTC upside; instead, the setup triggered during BTC distribution days where the initial strength faded quickly.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC above short-term trend with HYPE spot above SMA and OI stable confirms a >2% BTC long move over 3-7 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: BTC listed-IV momentum confirmation variant (btc_spot_pct_vs_24h_sma>0, near 7d high, spot up >0.75% and IV up) returned 43% win. Losses occurred when the spot gain was modest and the IV uptick reflected hedging rather than momentum; no funding context was used, so the signal struggled in range-bound conditions.

HYPE relative OI breakout continuation (H-128) shows 100% win in 2 tests, with funding normalizing and spot holding. This specific variant captures institutional accumulation phase effectively. Worth letting it run more tests before promotion.

AMZN extreme funding crash below -20% with negative basis variant (H-259) is a bright spot in the convergence family, with 100% win rate in 3 tests. It targets reversion from deeply negative readings and avoids the positive-funding stagnation seen elsewhere. This variant could form the core of a salvaged AMZN signal.

BTC PM IV regime-relative compression (H-523) using z-score bottom 20% has 67% win rate over 16 tests, a significant improvement over absolute threshold variants. The regime-relative approach is proving much more reliable and should replace H-001 entirely.

journalEntry: Tonight we promoted five shadow-discovered one-touch NO edge variants from the mining run into forward testing, alongside a significant pivot in AMZN convergence: the new extreme-negative funding/basis refinement replaces the stale positive-funding thesis. We also addressed failing regime-absolute IV thresholds by switching to z-score compression for BTC PM IV, and added momentum/money-flow guards to the gold heatmap and cross-asset setups. Closed a large one-touch NO shadow block with +12.07% on ETH, and recorded a substantial 12.07% win from a recently resolved shadow. Raised the FUNDING_EXTREME_LONG stop from 2% to 2.5% to allow more room given the signal's mean-reversion nature — the tighter stop was whipsawing trades, especially on GOLD and HYPE. Overall, the weekend funding reversion engine remains our cash cow, while we systematically cull the shadow heatmaps that failed forward.
